units.stage2_answer: Retain the short chapter route and force requirement: deleting them leaves the spike definition detached from the reason to learn it. Spike and firing rate are explained before motor action. Hertz is immediately translated to spikes per second; the average-rate qualification is needed.

Retain the physical pathway: extraocular means outside the eyeball in the same sentence; OMNs are expanded and connected to muscles; torque is explained as a turning effect. Muscle and cranial nerve names identify real parts and their connections, rather than carrying an unexplained argument. All six muscles are useful orientation context, though only the horizontal pair supports the later calculation. Shortening the remaining inventory would be optional, not a required order repair.

Retain repeated activation, tonic firing and the pulse-and-step explanation: deleting these loses the answer to how short spikes can produce lasting force. Saccade and tonic firing are explained at introduction. Neural drive means the continuing motor activation just described. Each mechanical term has a distinct job and is needed to rule out the idea that inertia holds a stationary eye. The concluding two sentences restate the distinction once before changing to coding.

Retain the question linking physical action to represented angle. Synapse, excitatory and inhibitory input, recurrent connectivity and tuning curve are established before the model relies on them. The code-to-action transition needs this distinction: a pattern representing an angle and the muscles holding it are different parts of the account. The tuning range caveat cannot be deleted without changing the model claim.

Retain population code, encoding and decoding because they distinguish the pattern from how a value is supplied or read. Neuron identity versus physical location prevents a specific wrong reading of the vector. Place fields and grid fields are established as the second application with the relevant anatomical differences, rather than repeating the eye pathway.

Retain the short reminder at the chapter boundary: the opening uses holding force to motivate the gap between stable activities and a stored value. The chapter route identifies what is added, and the first section link gives direct access to the moved explanation. These reminders do not reteach the six muscles or spike summation. Deleting all reminders would weaken the reason for the mechanics calculation; no required duplicate passage remains.

Retain the calculation as the quantitative extension of Chapter 1 rather than a second basic mechanics explanation. Its symbols are defined beside it. Oculomotor integrator is explained by what it accumulates and maintains. Plasticity is explained as lasting experience-dependent change before the goldfish example. The distinction between rapid mechanics and slower calibration is needed; the limits of the approximation and experiment remain necessary.

Retain the question that separates persistence of a pattern from correctness of its stored angle. It identifies the next model purpose using terms already introduced. The next paragraph answers that question; this is a brief question-and-mechanism connection, not repeated anatomy.

Retain the updated link and compact pathway reminder: the later empirical chapter needs to connect the maintained coordinate to measured movement. The OMN acronym is re-expanded after a chapter gap; abducens nucleus and ocular plant add recording-site and mechanical-system meanings here, so they do not duplicate the earlier nerve definition.
